newsitem.title: USA: Pepsi's Taco Bell has no plans to expand menu - exec.
newsitem.headline: Pepsi's Taco Bell has no plans to expand menu - exec.

text.p: A senior executive with PepsiCo's Taco Bell said the fast-food company does not plan to expand its menu to compete in the "burger wars" among major hamburger chains.

"We are enhancing the quality of our food and relaunching the same menu items with a greater emphasis on taste, quality and (restaurant) ambience," Joaquin Pelaez, a senior vice president of the company said in an interview. "We do not plan to introduce any new items."
He said Taco Bell's 1997 sales should be strong.

"Our numbers are pretty good. I think we're turning the business around," Pelaez said in a brief interview after addressing a food conference. "I think we're going to have a very strong year and I'm very optimistic."

In January, Pepsico announced it would spin off its restaurant business -- Taco Bell, KFC and Pizza Hut -- to shareholders by year-end. Wall Street analysts had said the restaurants were not been performing as well as expected.
